/api/pages.title: Research/Local AI workspace
/api/pages.content:
A practical starting point for a useful, private AI workspace — with clear boundaries between conversation, tools, and the things you keep.

> **The goal:** ask naturally, use the right tool, and save a result you can return to.

## The building blocks

| Layer | What it does | A useful default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Conversation** | Turn a question into a clear next step | Keep context close to the task |
| **Tools** | Search, calculate, convert, and act | Enable the integrations you need |
| **Memory** | Remember preferences and useful facts | Keep personal and operational data distinct |
| **Canvas** | Keep research, notes, and finished work | Save a readable page with its sources |

## From a question to a saved result

1. **Start with intent.** Explain what you want to learn or make.
2. **Gather the evidence.** Search, inspect a file, or use an enabled integration.
3. **Make it useful.** Compare the options and keep the details that matter.
4. **Save it here.** A Canvas page gives the result a home beyond the chat.

## A small checklist for the next project

- [x] Choose the tools and data sources the project needs.
- [x] Keep credentials in private configuration.
- [x] Save source links alongside conclusions.
- [ ] Turn the repeatable steps into a scheduled workflow.

<summary>Reference links and implementation notes</summary>

### Explore the components

- [Ollama](https://github.com/ollama/ollama) — a local model runtime.
- [Open WebUI](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui) — a browser interface for AI workflows.
- [Qdrant](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant) — a vector search engine.

These links are examples for a saved research page. Select services to fit your own setup.
